name: ip
one_line: show and change network addresses, routes and interfaces
plain: `ip` is the modern Linux tool to look at and change networking: your network cards (links), their addresses, the route table that decides where packets go, and the neighbour (ARP) table.

It works in objects: `ip addr`, `ip link`, `ip route`, `ip neigh`, `ip netns`. Each object has verbs: show, add, del, set. Plain `ip addr` means `ip addr show`. Most objects can be shortened (`ip a`, `ip r`, `ip l`).
It replaces the old ifconfig, route and arp commands.
when: Find your own IP address and which interface a VPN created.
See the default gateway and routing table.
Bring an interface up or down.
Add a temporary address or route in a lab.
Check the ARP table for neighbours on the LAN.

examples.title: Show all addresses
examples.explain: Lists every interface with its IPv4 (inet) and IPv6 (inet6) addresses. Look for the interface that has 10.x or 192.168.x.

examples.title: Short and brief view
examples.explain: -br prints one line per interface: name, state (UP/DOWN) and addresses. The easiest way to read it.

examples.title: Routing table
examples.explain: Shows where traffic goes. The line starting default via is your gateway.

examples.title: Which route would be used?
examples.explain: Asks the kernel how it would reach that address: the interface, the gateway and the source address it would use. Perfect for 'why does my VPN not work?'.

examples.title: Neighbours (ARP table)
examples.explain: Shows IP to MAC pairs the machine has recently talked to on the local network.

examples.title: Bring an interface up or down
examples.cmd:
sudo ip link set eth0 up
sudo ip link set eth0 down
examples.explain: link set changes the interface state. Needs root.

examples.title: Add and remove a temporary address
examples.cmd:
sudo ip addr add 192.168.56.10/24 dev eth1
sudo ip addr del 192.168.56.10/24 dev eth1
examples.explain: Handy in a lab. Changes disappear at reboot.

examples.title: Add a route
examples.explain: Tells the machine to send traffic for 10.20.x.x through the gateway 192.168.56.1.

examples.title: Live changes
examples.explain: Prints a line each time an address, link or route changes. Useful when a VPN connects.

options.plain: Object: protocol addresses on an interface. Verbs: show, add, del, flush.
Object: network devices. Verbs: show, set up/down, set mtu, set name, add (vlan, bridge, veth...).
Object: routing table. Verbs: show, add, del, get, replace, flush.
Show help; `ip addr help` gives help for an object.

mistakes: Setting an address with ip addr add and expecting it to survive a reboot: it does not.
Forgetting the prefix length (/24): without it ip assumes /32.
Assuming ifconfig exists: on a minimal Kali or Ubuntu it may not be installed.
Bringing down the interface you are connected over.
Reading only the first line of ip route: multiple routes decide where traffic goes.
try: Run ip -br addr and say which interface is your VPN.
Use ip route get on a lab IP and on 8.8.8.8 and compare.
Run ip monitor in one terminal and connect your VPN in another.
see_also: ss(8), ping(8), traceroute(8), nmcli(1), resolvectl(1), ifconfig(8), route(8), arp(8).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
